Sleep tracking and small routine changes can clarify what helps or disrupts rest.

## PLEASE Body Care {#please-body-care}

PLEASE connects physical care with emotional stability. The overview below is shared here once and supports related [Emotion Regulation](/learn/emotion-regulation/) lessons.

### Treat Physical Illness {#treat-physical-illness}

Attend to physical health concerns, take prescribed medication as directed, and contact a health-care provider when needed.

### Balanced Eating {#balanced-eating}

Eat regularly and adequately. Notice whether restriction, overeating, dehydration, or long gaps between meals increase emotional vulnerability.

### Avoid Mood-Altering Substances {#avoid-mood-altering-substances}

Avoid non-prescribed mood-altering substances and follow the plan agreed on with a qualified prescriber for medications.

### Balanced Sleep {#balanced-sleep}

Aim for the amount of sleep that supports your functioning. Keep wake time and bedtime reasonably consistent, and use the sleep practice sheet to test what helps.

### Exercise {#exercise}

Use regular movement that fits your health, mobility, and ability. Small, repeatable activity counts.

## Sleep Practice {#sleep-practice}

- Track bedtime, estimated time to fall asleep, waking during the night, final wake time, and time out of bed.
- Note naps, caffeine or other substances, medication timing, exercise, and major stressors.
- Choose one sleep-supporting change at a time and observe the pattern over several days.
- If sleep problems are persistent, severe, or connected with a medical or mental-health concern, bring the record to a qualified health-care provider.
